claim_boundaries.VC15: Successful context read finishes commit/connection close before worker creation. Failed/timeout context raises before worker launch. Do not generalize to all server-side work being gone when an aborted bridge child is reaped.
claim_boundaries.VC18: Exact durable state preservation verified for this timeout; it does not imply automatic PostgreSQL backend cancellation.
claim_boundaries.lifecycle_gate: Immediate backend execution termination on bridge timeout remains unproved and is contradicted by this deliberate sleeping-query fixture until explicit cleanup.
claim_boundaries.resource_caps: 20CPU/2GiBAS cap applies to Python child, not PostgreSQL backend query CPU/memory. No claims about backend CPU exhaustion or all possible long queries.

observed.exact_cancel_send_timestamp: not instrumented; cannot infer a more precise instant
observed.interval_caveat: Lower bound is recorded child reap time. Upper bound conservatively uses full group duration, which starts before child launch and includes final snapshot. Actual pg_sleep start/elapsed duration was not timestamped.

read_only_source_findings: Proxy FRAME_SECONDS=30 limits individual protocol reads, not PostgreSQL statement execution.
Proxy relay cancels Python relay tasks and closes backend transport; close() does not issue an automatic backend CancelRequest.
Validation-context SQL installs REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY and scope, with no statement_timeout setting. Canonical DSN helper sets startup options empty.

Owned postmaster launch options contain no timeout override; postgresql.auto.conf contains no setting; postgresql.conf has commented statement_timeout=0 default only. Actual runtime/role/database setting was not queried in this addendum.
SQL guard exact SAFE_SET admits timeout values=0; introducing nonzero timeouts is a separate reviewed policy/contract change.
Java DocumentGateway waits20s and reaps child through FrameProcess; DocumentQueries creates/launches DocumentWorker only after DocumentValidationContext.read returns successfully.
